reason: The hypothesis makes multiple specific claims about MSRO formation, evolution, and its role in governing plastic deformation in HEA multilayers, but cites no prior evidence whatsoever to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the claimed behavior of strain-induced MSRO in HEA multilayers.
premises: Strain-induced short-range order (MSRO) can form at FCC/BCC HEA multilayer interfaces under sustained loading
Initial MSRO regions act as barriers impeding dislocation motion
MSRO regions coarsen under sustained loading and facilitate activation of additional slip systems and twinning
MSRO evolution balances high strength with increasing ductility while maintaining nanoscale architecture
The proposed mechanism is specific to HEA multilayers with inherent lattice distortion and low initial MSRO
